content.value_statement: Astronomy work often needs precise coordinates, units, time systems, and FITS handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Astropy workflows for reliable scientific analysis.
actual_capabilities: Convert physical quantities with astropy.units and domain equivalencies.
Transform SkyCoord objects between ICRS, Galactic, FK5, and AltAz frames.
Read, inspect, and write FITS images and tables with Astropy tools.
Calculate cosmological distances, ages, lookback times, and model comparisons.
Handle precise Time objects, time scales, Julian dates, and time arithmetic.
Use WCS metadata to convert between image pixels and sky coordinates.
limitations: Requires Astropy and optional dependencies in the user Python environment.
Examples assume the user has permission to access each local or remote data file.
Does not replace review of scientific assumptions, calibrations, or chosen cosmology.
Remote data examples depend on network access and server availability.

use_cases.title: Process Telescope FITS Data
use_cases.description: Inspect HDU structure, read image arrays, review headers, and prepare data for analysis.

use_cases.title: Build Catalog Workflows
use_cases.description: Read tables, attach units, filter rows, join catalogs, and cross-match sky positions.

use_cases.title: Teach Astronomy Calculations
use_cases.description: Explain coordinate frames, cosmological distances, time scales, and unit conversions with practical examples.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Units
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Astropy units to convert my astronomy quantity. Explain the unit choice and show the final value with units.

prompt_templates.title: Transform Coordinates
prompt_templates.prompt: Transform these sky coordinates between the requested frames. Include required time, location, and unit assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect FITS Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect this FITS file workflow. Identify HDUs, important headers, image statistics, and safe file handling steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Analysis Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Astropy analysis plan that combines FITS input, WCS conversion, table matching, time handling, and uncertainty checks.

output_examples.input: Convert 15 parsecs to light years and explain why units matter.
output_examples.output: The response gives the converted distance, keeps units attached, and explains dimensional consistency in plain language.

output_examples.input: Plan a workflow to read a FITS image and report basic statistics.
output_examples.output: The response outlines opening the file safely, checking HDUs, selecting image data, reading headers, and summarizing statistics.

output_examples.input: Compare luminosity distance at redshift 1.5 with two cosmology models.
output_examples.output: The response names the selected cosmology models, describes the distance calculation, and warns that model choice affects results.

best_practices: Attach units to quantities early and keep them through calculations.
Use context managers when reading or updating FITS files.
State coordinate frames, time scales, observer location, and cosmology assumptions explicitly.
anti_patterns: Mixing unitless arrays with physical quantities without validation.
Changing FITS structural keywords without understanding the file format.
Using remote data files without confirming source trust and access permission.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps use Astropy for astronomy units, coordinates, FITS files, tables, cosmology, time systems, and WCS workflows.

faq.question: Does it install Astropy automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user controls package installation in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it work with FITS files?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers reading, writing, inspecting HDUs, handling headers, and working with FITS image or table data.

faq.question: Can it query online astronomy services?
faq.answer: It can explain Astropy patterns that use remote resources, but network access depends on the user environment and permissions.

faq.question: Is it useful for teaching?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain coordinate frames, units, time scales, WCS concepts, and cosmological calculations step by step.

faq.question: What should users verify?
faq.answer: Users should verify data provenance, coordinate frames, time scales, file permissions, and scientific assumptions before publishing results.
